question: What happens from opening a project to seeing an agent's edit light up?
tldr: Each agent turn: snapshot, edit, light up the map, check, repeat.
answer: The server watches the project and pushes changes to the page. Each chat turn is snapshotted before and after, and when the agent stops cockpit checks .cockpit/ and the guardrails and may send it back.
rate: once per chat message to the agent
why: The order of snapshot, live recording, checks and send-back is spread over serve, chat and recorder.

nodes.label: Open project
nodes.tldr: Desktop or CLI starts a server
nodes.explain: The desktop app (or npm run serve) starts one server for the project folder and shows the page.

nodes.label: Project state
nodes.tldr: Description, index, files and git, kept fresh
nodes.explain: What the server holds and pushes to the page as patches: .cockpit/ diagrams, the code index, git status, the running turn and the checks' results.

nodes.label: User message
nodes.tldr: You ask the agent for something
nodes.explain: A message typed in the chat panel, sent to the server and on to the agent.

nodes.label: Open a turn
nodes.tldr: Snapshot the code before the agent acts
nodes.explain: A commit of the whole work tree is made in cockpit's own git store, so the turn can later be diffed.

nodes.label: Claude edits
nodes.tldr: Claude Code works; each edited file is noted
nodes.explain: The Agent SDK runs Claude Code. Every tool call that touches a file is recorded and pushed, so the map lights up that box.

nodes.label: Check on stop
nodes.explain: When the agent stops after editing files, cockpit checks the description against the live code index and runs the guardrail checks.

nodes.label: Close the turn
nodes.explain: A second snapshot closes the turn and the page can show what it changed. Problems send the agent back instead, up to 3 times.

nodes.label: Window closed
nodes.explain: Closing the desktop window stops every project server it started.
